heading: Learn Hindi, from the script to C1.
lead: A complete course in the standard Hindi of India, written in Devanagari, for English speakers. The first tier is the script and its sounds; after it come gender and agreement, postpositions and the oblique case, the dative constructions, the ने construction and compound verbs, one step at a time. Every answer gets feedback that says why, and every Hindi word can be tapped for its forms and meaning.
fineprint: The whole course, the grammar reference, word practice and the placement test are free. Specializations, stories, conversation practice and the other extras are part of Premium, €8.99 a month or €69.99 a year.

panel.label: The course, tier by tier

items.title: 1 · Script and sounds
items.text: Devanagari vowels, consonants and conjuncts, the inherent vowel, greetings, तू, तुम and आप, होना.

items.title: 2 · First sentences
items.text: Gender and plurals, postpositions and the oblique case, का, के and की, the present habitual.

items.title: 3 · The verb system
items.text: The continuous, the future, को, मुझे चाहिए and other dative constructions, लाख and करोड़.

items.title: 4 · Building fluency
items.text: The ने construction, the subjunctive, ability and obligation, comparison, ही, भी and तो.

items.title: 5 · Everyday fluency
items.text: Compound and conjunct verbs, the conjunctive participle, relative-correlative clauses, conditionals.

items.title: 6 · Intermediate
items.text: Participles, the passive, causatives, reported speech, the presumptive.

items.title: 7 · Upper intermediate
items.text: Word formation, formal address, echo words, verb government, official Hindi.

items.title: 8 · Advanced
items.text: Tense and aspect, word order and particles, Hindi and Urdu, spoken Hindi, literature.

panel.note: 78 modules in eight tiers, plus 13 professional specializations with 117 more modules.

sections.heading: Hindi grammar explained, not guessed at

items.title: The script first, and in full
items.text: Tier 1 teaches Devanagari: the vowels and their signs, the consonants, conjuncts and nasals, the inherent vowel that is written but often not said, and the sounds English lacks, such as aspirated and retroflex consonants. A romanisation helps only in Tier 1; from Tier 2 on, the course writes Hindi in Devanagari alone.

items.title: Typing without a Hindi keyboard
items.text: Hindi typed in Latin letters turns into Devanagari as you type, and an on-screen Devanagari keyboard has every letter and sign.

items.title: Who is the subject
items.text: The dative constructions (मुझे चाहिए, मुझे हिंदी आती है) come in Tier 3, the perfective with intransitive verbs before the ने construction in Tier 4, and agreement with the object is explained where it happens.

items.title: Feedback that says why
items.text: Every answer gets feedback with the reason and a link to the grammar rule. Answers accept the spelling variants Hindi print really uses, such as हिन्दी for हिंदी.

items.title: Speaking with pronunciation feedback
items.text: Hindi has pronunciation assessment, so every core module has a speaking activity where you say words and sentences and get feedback on each word. Tier 1 has the most, on aspiration, retroflexes, vowel length and nasal vowels.

items.title: Common traps
items.text: Twelve short sets on the mistakes English speakers make, from letters that look alike, short and long vowels and the silent a to तुम and आप, the forgotten oblique, ने and agreement, and compound verbs.

items.question: Is the Hindi course free?
items.answer: Yes. All 78 modules from the script to C1, the grammar reference, word practice, the common traps and the placement test are free, with 5 Ask AI questions a day. Premium adds the specializations, stories, conversation practice and the other extras.

items.question: Do I need to know Devanagari first?
items.answer: No. Tier 1 teaches the script from the first vowel, with a romanisation beside the Hindi in that tier only.

items.question: Which Hindi does it teach?
items.answer: The standard Hindi of India, as educated speakers write and speak it: the Hindi of newspapers, television news, schoolbooks and everyday conversation. Tier 8 adds Hindi and Urdu and the layers of Hindi vocabulary, spoken Hindi and Hinglish, and the languages of the Hindi belt for recognition.

items.question: Are there practice papers for a Hindi exam?
items.answer: No. There is no widely recognised Hindi exam for foreign learners whose format its board publishes, so the course has no exam papers.

items.question: I already know some Hindi. Do I have to start at the beginning?
items.answer: No. Take the placement test and start at the tier it suggests.

closing.heading: Start with the script, or with the placement test.
